title: The Chiral Isomers of Chlorogenic Acid Exert Distinct Antiviral Effects on Coxsackievirus A16 Infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: Coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16) is one of the major pathogens responsible for hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD), for which no specific antiviral therapy is currently available.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study investigated the antiviral effects of Neochlorogenic acid (NCGA) and chlorogenic acid (CGA) against CVA16, with a focus on their distinct biological activities.
analysis.methods: The study employed in vitro and in vivo assays to evaluate the antiviral activity of NCGA and CGA against CVA16, including RNA-binding motif protein 24 (RBM24) knockdown experiments to identify host factors involved.
analysis.main_results: In our study, we found that NCGA exhibited antiviral activity against CVA16, whereas CGA was completely inactive.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Collectively, our findings not only identify a novel natural product against CVA16 but also provide clues for the discovery of host factors involved in CVA16 infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Our findings suggest that NCGA could be a promising candidate for the development of antiviral therapies targeting CVA16, which is a significant pathogen in HFMD.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study provides moderate confidence in its findings due to the limited scope of the in vitro and in vivo experiments, though the results are supported by direct observations and host factor identification.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the antiviral effects of chiral isomers of chlorogenic acid, specifically Neochlorogenic acid (NCGA) and chlorogenic acid (CGA), against Coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16). The research highlights that NCGA exhibits antiviral activity against CVA16, while CGA is inactive. The study also identifies RNA-binding motif protein 24 (RBM24) as a host factor involved in NCGA's antiviral effect. These findings suggest NCGA could be a potential therapeutic agent for CVA16 infections, which are a major cause of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD). The study's results are supported by direct observations and in vivo experiments, though the evidence is limited to the specific context of CVA16 and does not extend to other related viruses. The evidence is considered moderate in strength due to the study's design and the need for further validation.

title: Seroprevalence of EV-A71 and EV-D68 antibodies in the paediatric and adolescent population, France, 2023 to 2025

analysis.research_question_and_background: Enteroviruses (EV)-A71 and EV-D68 are potentially associated with severe clinical conditions, especially in infants and young children. Population susceptibility to these viruses is unknown in France.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A stratified sampling approach based on sex, age and geographical area of residence was applied to obtain sera for routine diagnostic from ˂ 18-year-olds in metropolitan France. A total of 501 serum samples collected between 2023 and 2025 from 0-17-year-olds were included in the investigation.
analysis.methods: Neutralising activity was tested against EV-A71 sub-genogroup C1 and EV-D68 subclade B3 strains isolated in 2016, allowing to determine seropositivity and nAb titre.
analysis.main_results: For EV-A71, the overall estimated seroprevalence was 43.7% (95% CI: 39.3-48.2) while for EV-D68 this reached 96.0% (95% CI: 93.9-97.5). No differences according to sex were observed. Unlike EV-D68, EV-A71 seropositivity rate varied significantly by age group (p = 0.002) and area of residence (p < 0.001). Notably, 23 of 25 children aged ˂ 1 year lacked EV-A71 protective antibodies. Significant differences occurred across age groups both for EV-A71 (p = 0.004) and EV-D68 (p < 0.001). The nAb titres appeared as highest in 1 to under-2-year-olds for EV-A71 and 0 to under-1-year-olds for EV-D68.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This seroprevalence study in France reveals a high proportion of newborns and infants susceptible to EV-A71 at potential risk of severe disease, contrasting with the high level of immunity against EV-D68 across all paediatric age groups.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for targeted surveillance and prevention strategies for EV-A71 in young children, while suggesting that EV-D68 may be less of a concern due to high immunity levels.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and reliance on routine diagnostic sera, which may not represent the entire population. The evidence is moderate as it is based on seroprevalence data without longitudinal or causal analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the seroprevalence of EV-A71 and EV-D68 neutralising antibodies among children and adolescents in France from 2023 to 2025. It found that EV-D68 had a high seroprevalence rate of 96.0% (95% CI: 93.9-97.5), while EV-A71 had a lower rate of 43.7% (95% CI: 39.3-48.2). Notably, 23 of 25 children under one year lacked EV-A71 protective antibodies, indicating significant susceptibility in this age group. The results showed that EV-A71 seropositivity varied by age and geographical area, whereas EV-D68 seropositivity was consistent across all age groups. The study highlights the potential risk of severe disease from EV-A71 in young children, contrasting with the high immunity observed against EV-D68. The findings suggest the need for targeted surveillance and prevention strategies for EV-A71, while indicating that EV-D68 may be less of a public health concern. The study's cross-sectional design and use of routine diagnostic sera limit the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate.

title: Enterovirus 2C Protein Drug Design, Assay Development, and Drug Resistance Studies.

analysis.methods: The researchers employed medicinal chemistry, molecular pharmacology, resistance profiling, structural modeling, and assay development, including a fluorescence polarization-based binding assay to monitor ligand engagement of the conserved allosteric pocket in enteroviral 2C proteins.
analysis.main_results: The initial studies led to quinoline-based antivirals with improved potency and selectivity against EV-D68, and subsequent development of pyrazolopyridine-based inhibitors resulted in one of the most potent classes of enteroviral 2C inhibitors reported to date.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Mechanistic studies confirmed direct engagement of a conserved allosteric pocket in enteroviral 2C proteins, supporting the feasibility of chemically targeting this protein for antiviral development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide a foundation for the development of clinically useful antivirals targeting enteroviral 2C proteins, which could be significant for managing enterovirus infections such as EV-D68-induced paralysis.

The results provide strong pharmacological validation for 2C as a therapeutic target, which could lead to new treatments for enterovirus infections. title: Deciphering Viral Antigenic Relationships Through Antigenic Cartography: A Narrative Review

analysis.scope_and_question: Antigenic cartography is a computational approach that quantitatively visualizes antigenic relationships among viral strains using serological data, including hemagglutination inhibition and virus-neutralization assays. Since its introduction in the early 2000s, it has substantially advanced the study of viral antigenic evolution by transforming complex serological measurements into interpretable antigenic maps, thereby facilitating assessment of antigenic diversity, immune escape, cross-reactivity, and vaccine–virus relationships.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The literature was synthesized comparatively across major applications of antigenic cartography, encompassing human seasonal influenza and other viruses, including dengue, lyssaviruses, foot-and-mouth disease virus, Enterovirus A71, norovirus, rotavirus, SARS-CoV-2, and HIV. Particular attention was given to real-world applications, methodological advances, sources of uncertainty, and integration with genomic, structural, evolutionary, and computational approaches.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Influenza remains the most extensively studied viral pathogen, where antigenic cartography has supported recognition of epidemiologically relevant antigenic transitions and informed vaccine decisions. Examples include the emergence of A/Fujian/411/2002-like H3N2 viruses during 2004–2005 and assessment of A/California/07/2009 during 2010–2011. Applications to other viruses demonstrate broader utility for characterizing antigenic landscapes and evaluating cross-protective immunity and vaccine performance.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Map reliability is influenced by serological assay variability, serum-panel composition, measurement noise, incomplete and geographically biased datasets. Limited inter-operability among serological, genomic, and structural datasets further restricts reproducibility and cross-study comparability.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future platforms should incorporate standardized and automated serological measurements, inter-laboratory calibration, harmonized data standards, geographically representative datasets, experimental validation, and interpretable continuously updated models. Integration of artificial intelligence, protein language models, evolutionary modelling, structural vaccinology, and real-time genomic–serological surveillance could enable earlier prediction of antigenic drift, identification of emerging vaccine mismatches, and prioritization of candidate vaccine strains.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the use of antigenic cartography in understanding viral antigenic relationships, particularly focusing on human enteroviruses. Antigenic cartography is a computational method that uses serological data to visualize antigenic relationships among viral strains, aiding in the study of antigenic evolution. The review highlights the application of this technique in influenza, where it has been instrumental in identifying antigenic transitions and guiding vaccine decisions. While the method has broader utility for other viruses, including enteroviruses, challenges such as assay variability, dataset incompleteness, and limited interoperability among data types hinder its effectiveness. The review emphasizes the need for standardized serological measurements, harmonized data standards, and integration with genomic and structural approaches to improve reproducibility and cross-study comparability. Future directions include leveraging artificial intelligence and real-time genomic-serological surveillance to enhance predictive capabilities and vaccine strain prioritization.

title: Một số đặc điểm dịch tễ học bệnh tay chân miệng tại khu vực miền Bắc Việt Nam giai đoạn 2024 – 2025 Epidemiological Characteristics of Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease in Northern Vietnam, 2024–2025

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nghiên cứu được thực hiện nhằm mô tả các đặc điểm dịch tễ học của bệnh tay chân miệng (TCM) tại miền Bắc Việt Nam và mối liên quan giữa tình trạng bệnh nặng với các yếu tố dịch tễ, đồng thời phân bố các tác nhân vi rút đường ruột trong các mẫu bệnh phẩm được xét nghiệm.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Đây là một nghiên cứu hồi cứu, phân tích dữ liệu từ 18 tỉnh/thành phố miền Bắc Việt Nam trong giai đoạn 2024–2025, bao gồm danh sách ca bệnh TCM và 124 mẫu phân hoặc dịch họng từ các ca bệnh có độ lâm sàng 2b trở lên hoặc tại ổ dịch.
analysis.methods: Dữ liệu được thu thập từ Hệ thống báo cáo bệnh truyền nhiễm và phân tích bằng phương pháp realtime RT-PCR tại Viện Vệ sinh dịch tễ Trung ương. Các ca bệnh được phân loại theo độ lâm sàng và đánh giá bằng phân tích đa biến để xác định các yếu tố liên quan đến tình trạng bệnh nặng.
analysis.main_results: Có 30.136 ca TCM đủ tiêu chuẩn, không tử vong. Năm 2025 ghi nhận 16.629 ca (35,9 ca/100.000 dân), tăng 23,1% so với 13.507 ca năm 2024 (29,4 ca/100.000 dân). Trẻ ≤6 tuổi chiếm 97,9% (28.695/29.293 ca). Nam giới chiếm 63,2% (19.061/30.136 ca). Độ lâm sàng 1-2a chiếm 98,4% (18.109/18.410 ca).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Năm 2025 có tỷ lệ bệnh nặng cao hơn so với năm 2024, với aOR = 1,55 và khoảng tin cậy 95% là 1,21–1,99. Điều này cho thấy có sự thay đổi đáng kể trong xu hướng dịch bệnh.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Nghiên cứu cung cấp thông tin quan trọng về xu hướng gia tăng của TCM trong thời gian gần đây, đặc biệt là ở trẻ em dưới 6 tuổi, từ đó nhấn mạnh nhu cầu khôi phục giám sát trọng điểm và chuẩn hóa dữ liệu để phòng chống dịch hiệu quả.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Dữ liệu được thu thập từ Hệ thống báo cáo bệnh truyền nhiễm, có thể bị ảnh hưởng bởi độ chính xác của báo cáo. Tuy nhiên, nghiên cứu có số lượng ca bệnh lớn và phân tích đa biến, cho thấy mức độ tin cậy cao.

analysis.summary_en: Nghiên cứu này mô tả các đặc điểm dịch tễ học của bệnh tay chân miệng (TCM) tại miền Bắc Việt Nam trong giai đoạn 2024–2025, bao gồm xu hướng gia tăng số ca bệnh, đặc điểm nhân khẩu học và phân bố tác nhân vi rút. Kết quả cho thấy TCM lưu hành quanh năm, đạt đỉnh vào tháng 3–4, với trẻ em dưới 6 tuổi chiếm tỷ lệ cao nhất. Năm 2025 ghi nhận 16.629 ca, tăng 23,1% so với năm 2024. Phân tích đa biến cho thấy năm 2025 có liên quan với tình trạng bệnh nặng, với aOR = 1,55 và khoảng tin cậy 95% là 1,21–1,99. Nghiên cứu cũng xác định 43/124 mẫu bệnh phẩm dương tính với vi rút đường ruột, trong đó CV-A16 chiếm tỷ lệ cao nhất (41,9%). Các kết quả này nhấn mạnh nhu cầu khôi phục giám sát trọng điểm và chuẩn hóa dữ liệu để hỗ trợ công tác phòng chống dịch. Mặc dù nghiên cứu dựa trên dữ liệu báo cáo, nhưng số lượng ca bệnh lớn và phương pháp phân tích đa biến cung cấp bằng chứng đáng tin cậy.
